parts: Lesson 8: Mailing and Messaging Services — Summary

E-mail (Electronic Mail) is the exchange of messages through digital devices via the internet; text, graphic, audio and video files can be sent as attachments. Advantages: send and receive from anywhere at any time (both must be connected and logged in); very fast; the same mail can go to many recipients; multiple files of any type can be attached; mails can be organised in folders.

An e-mail account gives a definite address such as user_student@gmail.com: user_student is the user name, gmail the service provider, .com the commercial domain and @ separates the user name and domain name. Providers: Gmail, Yahoo! Mail, Hotmail, Zoho Mail. Create a Gmail account: open a browser and type www.gmail.com, press Enter, click Create account, fill in the registration form (user name, password, name, address, date of birth, phone number), accept the terms and conditions. Sign in with a valid user name and password.

Inbox has three tabs: Primary (mails from people), Social (notifications from sites such as Twitter and LinkedIn) and Promotions (advertisements, offers). Unread mails are counted on the tab headers; mails are shown in reverse order of date (latest on top) with the sender, subject and time. Compose a mail: click Compose; the New Message window opens; type the recipient addresses (separate several by comma or semicolon); type the subject; type the message and format it; click Send (shortcut Ctrl+Enter) or Discard Draft to cancel. CC (carbon copy) sends a copy to another person; BCC (blind carbon copy) recipients are not visible to the other recipients. Reply sends a mail back to the sender (address filled automatically); Forward sends the same mail to another person.

Send an attachment: click Compose (or Reply/Forward), type the recipient, subject and message, click the Paperclip icon, browse and select the file and click Open (a progress bar shows uploading), then click Send; Gmail allows a maximum of 25 MB attachments. Download an attachment: a paperclip icon shows in the inbox; open the mail, click the Download icon; the file saves in the default download folder. Always log out (Sign Out) after work.

E-mail etiquette is the code of conduct for e-mail; good etiquette gives a good impression of the sender and organization and brings a prompt response. Composing: e-mail is not private so do not send confidential information; use a professional font; state the purpose in a short subject line; be careful with CC and BCC; do not use uppercase; be courteous with a suitable salutation (Dear, Mr., Ms.); avoid blaming, ambiguous statements, abbreviations and long introductions; begin with a greeting or thanks; mention attachments and compress large ones; end with a closing phrase and an official signature; review and spell-check before sending; keep antivirus updated. Replying: reply within 24 hours; do not reply to spam or likely fraud mails; answer queries precisely; scan attachments before downloading; do not overuse Reply to All.

Messaging service (Instant Messaging, IM): messages sent and received in real time over the internet through digital devices, using a messenger program; the sender and receiver generally know each other; when a messenger runs on a smartphone it is called an App. IM is an informal communication medium; e-mail is a formal one. Skype (launched 2003; owned by Microsoft): video conferencing, messaging, user profiles, online status, emoticons, chat history, job interviews, conference calls; used in education for virtual field trips and language exchange. Facebook Messenger (launched 2011): messages, pictures, audio and video calls, files; Messenger Kids (December 2017) for ages 6–12, managed by parents. WhatsApp: very popular mobile messaging (taken over by Facebook in February 2014): text, images, voice messages, voice and video calls, group chat and location sharing; needs a mobile number. WhatsApp Web (released January 2015) is a browser extension of the phone: open https://web.whatsapp.com, scan the QR code with the phone, which must be connected to the internet.
